about.title: Downey Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Downey's busiest commercial stretches — Firestone Boulevard, Lakewood Boulevard, Florence Avenue and Paramount Boulevard — are lined with grocery stores, strip-mall parking lots, restaurants and apartment complexes. Those are also the places where a wet entryway, a broken curb stop or a dim stairwell can send a person to the emergency room. When that happens in Downey, California law asks a fairly narrow question: did the property owner know about the hazard, or should they reasonably have known, and did they fail to fix it or warn about it? That element, called notice, decides most premises cases. Proving it depends on evidence that disappears fast. Surveillance footage is often overwritten within days, spills are mopped, and loose tiles get patched before anyone asks about them. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect people hurt on someone else's property in Downey with an independent personal injury attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out early gives the proof a chance to survive.

whyChoose.title: Why Downey Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: In California you generally have to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys in our network build that proof through inspection logs, employee statements and prior complaints.

items.title: Video Gets Erased — Act Before It Does
items.desc: Most Downey stores and apartment buildings keep surveillance for only a short window. An attorney can send a preservation demand right away so footage of your fall is not overwritten.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you are found partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by that percentage rather than eliminated. An independent attorney can push back when an owner overstates your share.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk in Downey. Who is responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who controls that stretch of sidewalk. If it belongs to the City of Downey or another public entity, California requires a government claim first, typically within six months of the injury, which is far shorter than the two years allowed against a private owner. If an adjacent business or property owner caused or maintained the defect, the analysis and timeline may differ. Getting the ownership question answered quickly matters.

items.question: The store manager said I was on my phone. Does that kill my case?
items.answer: No. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning a jury or adjuster can assign you a share of blame and reduce your compensation by that share, but your claim is not barred. The owner still has to answer for whether they knew about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can weigh how much your own conduct actually contributed.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Downey?
items.answer: Photograph the hazard and the surrounding area before it is cleaned or repaired, and get the names of anyone who saw you fall. Ask the business for an incident report and request that surveillance video be saved. See a doctor even if the pain seems minor, because some fractures and head injuries show up later. Then contact LawProactive so an attorney can send a formal preservation request.
